blindSummary:
This is a dangerous destination for transgender visitors, and one precedent case defines the record — in February 2021, two trans women — including a young well-known trans video creator (b. 1997) — were arrested in a restaurant in the country's main commercial city over their clothing, convicted of "attempted homosexuality," "indecent dressing" and identity-card irregularities, and sentenced to five years. They described five months of "hell" in that city's central prison, initially in leg chains, before release pending appeal; one later fled and received asylum abroad. A penal-code provision criminalises same-sex acts (up to five years), and this country has among the region's highest prosecution rates for such laws.

Police and mob violence against perceived LGBT people are both documented, and there is no legal gender recognition or protection of any kind. The 2021 conviction shows that visible trans expression in a public place is itself treated as a prosecutable offence.

For a visitor: visible trans presentation in public risks arrest on indecency/ID grounds; prison conditions are severe.
blindOutOfScope: Same-sex criminalisation is the statutory vehicle; the 2021 convictions demonstrate direct application to gender expression.
